stories.title: Delhi and Bihar launch subsidised bus services for Chhath Puja
stories.summary: Ahead of Chhath Puja, the Delhi and Bihar governments have launched 77 inter-state bus services to facilitate travel for residents heading home. Fares are subsidised by up to Rs 1,028. The initiative aims to ease the festive rush for people from Bihar and Poorvanchal living in Delhi.

stories.title: Mumbai leads India in green building registrations
stories.summary: Mumbai now has 2,057 projects registered with the Indian Green Building Council, an increase of 319 since last year. While Maharashtra leads the country with 4,754 total projects, the majority of Mumbai's registrations are commercial or residential. The green building movement remains heavily focused on premium developments.

stories.summary: Meta has signed purchase commitments for low-carbon cement, steel, and recycled plastics. The company will buy at least 180,000 tons of cement from Sublime Systems, which uses an electrochemical process to bypass the need for extreme heat. The deal supports a new commercial-scale facility in Massachusetts.

stories.title: CBI court denies bail to former Chandigarh Smart City CFO
stories.summary: A CBI court in Chandigarh has dismissed the bail application of Nalini Malik, the former CFO of Smart City Company Limited. Malik was arrested in April 2026 regarding an alleged scam involving over Rs 116 crore of city funds deposited in a private bank.

stories.title: Coimbatore courts to relocate to corporation building
stories.summary: Four courts will move to a Coimbatore Corporation commercial complex starting November 16, 2026. The relocation follows structural damage identified in the heritage building of the combined court complex. The affected courts include those handling CBI, corruption, and SC/ST cases.

stories.summary: Assam’s Garo Cultural Forum seeks CM’s intervention to preserve community heritage The Garo Cultural Forum submitted a memorandum to Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma during the Wangala Festival. stories.title: AUX Architecture completes performing arts center
stories.summary: AUX Architecture has completed the 10,550 square metre Glorya Kaufman Performing Arts Center. The project, finished in 2021, serves a site with a 114-year history that began as a cottage-style orphanage. The facility now hosts performance spaces, supported by a long list of materials and manufacturers.

stories.title: Demolition crew clears footpath outside TMC MP's home
stories.summary: Civic workers used a bulldozer to remove a temporary bamboo shed and dismantle an iron gate outside the residence of TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee on Thursday. Authorities stated the structures obstructed pedestrian movement. The MP noted that bulldozers could not resolve the underlying political situation.

stories.title: Cabinet approves museum project for North and South Blocks
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet has cleared a 3,230 crore rupee project to transform the North and South Blocks into the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum. Prime Minister Modi has expressed support for the initiative, which aims to repurpose the historic government buildings into a national cultural landmark.

stories.title: JNU building plans face design scrutiny
stories.summary: The Delhi Urban Art Commission has requested major revisions to two proposed buildings at Jawaharlal Nehru University. The commission cited deficiencies in parking, facade treatment, and utility planning. The proposals, submitted by the Central Public Works Department, require further design work before they can proceed.

stories.title: Novak Djokovic partners on Miami wellness tower
stories.summary: Aman is launching a new brand called ATMA in partnership with tennis player Novak Djokovic. The first project is a 1,049ft tower in Miami featuring a 120,000 sq ft wellness centre, racquet club and private residences. The group says the brand is built around longevity and performance.

stories.title: Hosoya Schaefer wins Bratislava harbor competition
stories.summary: Hosoya Schaefer Architects has won a masterplanning competition to transform Bratislava's Winter Harbour into a mixed-use district. The proposal aims to convert the industrial site into a neighborhood with residential buildings and public parks. The competition attracted 123 submissions from various international design firms.

stories.title: University of Miami to curate U.S. Pavilion
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of State has selected the University of Miami School of Architecture to curate the U.S. Pavilion at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale. The exhibition will focus on the laborers and craftspeople who build architectural structures, rather than the architects who design them.

stories.title: Foster + Partners begins work on Tennessee campus
stories.summary: Construction has started on a 4.5 billion dollar campus for Larry Ellison on the Cumberland River in Nashville. The 28-hectare site features five office clusters and a floating amphitheatre. A new bridge will connect the development to the nearby Germantown neighbourhood.

stories.title: Aman opens Baja California retreat
stories.summary: Aman has opened Amanvari, an 18-key property on Mexico's East Cape. The company describes the retreat as a study in desert minimalism, designed to offer privacy and connection to nature. The name translates to peace and water in Sanskrit, reflecting the brand's focus on serenity.

stories.title: Floating laboratory launched in Peruvian Amazon
stories.summary: CASA has completed a 60 square metre floating boat designed to provide healthcare and education services to dispersed communities in the Peruvian Amazon. The project addresses the difficulty of accessing basic services in the region, where river transport is the primary connection between riverside populations.

stories.title: Ecuadorian performance campus takes shape
stories.summary: The Bombódromo, a 10,000-seat performance campus in northern Ecuador, is currently under construction. Designed by Caá Porá Arquitectura and Jerome Haferd Studio, the project uses the traditional bomba drum as a generative design concept. The structure aims to integrate Afro-Ecuadorian heritage into its physical form.

stories.title: EMBT completes Naples metro station
stories.summary: EMBT has finished the Naples Underground Central Station, featuring a wavy timber roof designed to contrast with the surrounding 1970s business district. The 10,000-square-metre project aims to provide a more welcoming public plaza. The station is currently shortlisted for a 2026 infrastructure award.

stories.title: RooMoo repurposes mountain cabins into hotel
stories.summary: Chinese studio RooMoo has converted abandoned mountain cabins into the 24-room Cloudhaus Hotel on Jinfo Mountain. The project reused concrete drill cores and salvaged timber from the surrounding landscape. The building retains its original structure while adding a white-rendered facade with eight projecting frames.

stories.title: Old Street co-living tower receives planning approval
stories.summary: Hackney Council has approved a 35-storey co-living tower at Finsgate House. The development will provide 490 units and 4,000 square metres of workspace. Developers AHMM and HUB stated the existing 1980s buildings offered poor quality office space. Three councillors voted for the plan while four abstained.

stories.title: SOM wins Geelong pier competition
stories.summary: SOM has won the design competition for the Cunningham Pier in Geelong. The announcement follows the 2026 Sustainability Summit. Further details regarding the winning design proposal have not been released in the provided text. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Icon 3D-prints commercial building in San Antonio
stories.summary: Proptech startup Icon is currently 3D-printing a commercial building in San Antonio. The project marks a move into larger-scale commercial construction for the company. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Austin firm prints commercial building
stories.summary: An Austin-based company is 3D-printing its largest commercial building to date in San Antonio. The project utilizes the firm's proprietary printing technology. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Crosslam completes hybrid timber tower in Brazil
stories.summary: Crosslam has completed Aurora 275, a 22-metre hybrid building in São Paulo. The structure uses a reinforced concrete core combined with mass-timber elements. The company claims it is the tallest building of its type in Brazil, intended to demonstrate the potential of mass-timber construction.

stories.title: Melbourne office tower installs 1,391 solar panels
stories.summary: Developers have installed 1,391 solar panels into the facade and roof of a 48-story Melbourne office tower. The system is expected to supply 20 percent of the building’s base electricity demand. The project is billed as one of the world’s first large-scale solar facades on a commercial tower.

stories.title: Engineers burn timber ceilings to test fire safety
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Queensland are setting full-scale cross-laminated timber ceilings on fire to study structural collapse. The project aims to update safety guidance, as current standards often assume building structures will not burn. Timber is a load-bearing material that also acts as a fuel source.

stories.title: SecureTech subsidiary signs intent for 3D-printed home
stories.summary: SecureTech Innovations subsidiary AI UltraProd has signed a non-binding letter of intent to develop a 3D-printed residential project in Concord, California. The proposed plan aims to showcase the company's robotic construction technology, beginning with the construction of a single-story accessory dwelling unit.

stories.title: Researchers 3D print blocks from lunar dust
stories.summary: University of Arkansas researchers have 3D printed interlocking building blocks using lunar regolith simulant. The team sintered the powder directly using laser powder bed fusion without a binder. The blocks are not yet capable of bearing loads, but the method aims to reduce cargo requirements for Moon missions.

stories.title: 3D-printed concrete used to rebuild fire-damaged homes
stories.summary: A Dutch-made gantry crane is extruding concrete walls to rebuild a home in Altadena, California, following the 2025 Eaton Fire. The project is managed by Emergent Home, which plans to complete seven concrete-printed houses in the area. The builder was originally founded to assist with post-fire reconstruction efforts.

stories.title: Bio-based wood adhesive market projected to grow
stories.summary: The global market for bio-based structural wood adhesives is projected to reach $1.13 billion in 2026, representing a 9.7 percent growth rate. Demand is rising for sustainable building materials and prefabricated construction systems, with major firms like BASF and Dow driving the shift toward mass timber solutions.

stories.title: India and Norway discuss waste-to-resource construction
stories.summary: India and Norway are exploring joint research projects to convert industrial and construction waste into infrastructure materials. The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and Norway's SINTEF held a dialogue in New Delhi to discuss sustainable waste management solutions for the cement and construction sectors.

stories.title: Karnal sets year-end deadline for smart city projects
stories.summary: The Karnal Smart City agency has directed officials to complete all ongoing infrastructure projects by the end of December. The CEO of the agency instructed construction teams to expedite pending work on the city's stadium and other developments without compromising on the quality of the final output.

stories.title: Haryana orders flood management plan for Gurugram
stories.summary: The Haryana government has ordered an investigation into Gurugram's drainage issues and set a December 31 deadline for a flood management action plan. Officials must identify root causes of waterlogging and map vulnerable locations, moving beyond the current practice of clearing roads only after heavy rainfall occurs.

stories.title: UP RERA mandates homebuyer consent for plan changes
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Real Estate Regulatory Authority now requires promoters to obtain written consent from at least two-thirds of allottees before changing approved project plans. Promoters must share complete particulars of proposed modifications, and the authority plans to introduce a standard format for collecting these buyer approvals.

stories.title: Aquaculture startup raises $6 million for land-based farm
stories.summary: An aquaculture startup has raised $6 million to construct a land-based fish farm in Lee County. Further details regarding the project timeline and specific operational capacity are available in the full piece for subscribers.

stories.title: Hyderabad home registrations dip as transaction values rise
stories.summary: Hyderabad recorded 61,033 residential property registrations between January and October 2026, a 1 percent decline from the previous year. However, the total value of these transactions rose 3 percent to 44,305 crore rupees, reflecting a growing market contribution from higher-ticket homes, according to Knight Frank India.

stories.title: Consumer group seeks solar net-metering reform
stories.summary: A consumer advocacy group in Coimbatore has requested that the government improve rooftop solar net-metering terms. Under current rules, surplus electricity credits lapse without compensation on March 31. The group argues that these arrangements undermine incentives for households to act as prosumers of renewable energy.

stories.title: Landmark Group plans 1,600 crore investment in NCR
stories.summary: Landmark Group plans to invest 1,600 crore rupees to develop a 3 million square foot office complex in Gurugram and an integrated project on the Dwarka Expressway. The company recently raised 330 crore rupees in construction finance from SBI to support its expansion in the national capital region.

stories.title: Climate-smart design proposed to combat urban heat
stories.summary: Urban heat islands occur as concrete and glass absorb and release heat, causing cities to remain warmer than surrounding areas. Climate-smart buildings designed to work with local weather patterns are being proposed as a practical method to lower temperatures and improve endurance during harsh summer months.

stories.title: Mumbai ropeway project faces environmental hurdles
stories.summary: The Public Works Department has invited bids for an architectural design to connect Mulund to a temple inside the Sanjay Gandhi National Park. Construction within the park is legally prohibited unless explicitly for wildlife management, requiring the project to clear significant statutory hurdles before proceeding.

stories.title: Bihar approves new building bylaws
stories.summary: The Bihar cabinet has approved updated building bylaws for 2026, which include provisions for green building norms, rooftop solar installations, and water conservation. Investors and entrepreneurs have welcomed the move, which aims to support the development of modern satellite townships that meet global standards.

stories.title: Study links building clusters to cooler city blocks
stories.summary: Researchers at Sun Yat-sen and Ghent universities found that larger clusters of buildings serving similar purposes are associated with cooler ground surfaces. The study of 101 cities suggests that how buildings are grouped by use may be an overlooked factor in mitigating the urban heat island effect.

stories.title: Karachi opens first sponge park to manage rainwater
stories.summary: Karachi has inaugurated an experimental sponge park at Jamali Park to absorb, store, and reuse rainwater. The six-month project, developed with WWF-Pakistan, aims to reduce urban flooding and recharge groundwater. The city has decided to stop sending its water directly to the sea.

stories.title: New model predicts Dhaka flooding 24 hours in advance
stories.summary: Researchers have developed an operational flood forecasting system for Dhaka by coupling hydrological and hydraulic modeling. Published in Computational Urban Science, the study integrates weather predictions to forecast waterlogging and inundation one day ahead. The city remains one of the world's most vulnerable low-lying urban areas.

stories.summary: Utah startup Torus raised $500 million to launch Foundry, a line of prefabricated AI inference units. stories.summary: Equinix is accelerating its expansion in India, targeting enterprise demand for AI and cloud computing. The company has invested over $365 million in the region and aims to reach 14,000 racks by 2028. It entered the market in 2021 by acquiring GPX India.

stories.title: Zacua Ventures closes $135 million fund for physical industry tech
stories.summary: Zacua Ventures has closed its second fund at $135 million to invest in robotics, manufacturing, and energy. The firm is targeting technologies that transform the physical economy, including construction sites and data centers. The vast majority of its limited partners are construction firms and other strategics.

stories.title: Amy Catania Kulper appointed dean of University of Virginia School of Architecture
stories.summary: Amy Catania Kulper will become dean of the University of Virginia School of Architecture on January 6, 2027. Kulper most recently led the Bartlett School of Architecture at University College London. She succeeds Malo Hutson, who will return to the faculty after serving in the role since 2021.

stories.title: Advice for architecture students
stories.summary: Architecture students face high fees, reduced contact time, and the influence of AI. They also navigate low graduate salaries and a cost of living crisis. While the field is described as a brilliant educational opportunity, many students are currently living at home. The path is shifting.

stories.title: The need for new models of ageing
stories.summary: Retirement can lead to a sense of monotony for older adults despite financial security. New approaches to ageing suggest that engaging in visual puzzles, news discussions, and creative challenges can provide a different energy. The current model of unstructured leisure may not be enough for everyone.

stories.title: David Brian Hill named dean of University of Houston architecture college
stories.summary: David Brian Hill will become the next dean of the Gerald D. Hines College of Architecture and Design at the University of Houston on February 1, 2027. Hill, a veteran educator and researcher, succeeds Patricia Belton Oliver. The college describes itself as being on a great trajectory.

stories.title: Amy Kulper named UVA School of Architecture dean
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Amy Catania Kulper has been named the next dean of the University of Virginia School of Architecture, effective January 6. She joins the university following her tenure as head of the Bartlett School of Architecture at University College London.

research.title: Scientists squeeze record-breaking X-ray power into an incredibly tiny spot
research.summary: Scientists have created record-breaking X-ray flashes lasting just 300 attoseconds, concentrating enormous power into an incredibly tiny spot. The breakthrough could unlock a new way to observe electrons in action and potentially control the ultrafast processes that drive chemical reactions.

research.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
research.summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
